summary:
We developed Korol-on, an integrated astronaut health monitoring and mission support application designed to improve crew safety and well-being during space missions.
Unlike basic health tracking apps, Korol-on combines multiple aspects of astronaut care in one platform. It allows crew members to manage personal medical profiles and monitor vital signs, sleep, physical activity, nutrition, hydration, stress levels, and radiation exposure while tracking health trends over time.
The application features Korolov-AI, an intelligent digital companion that provides personalized wellness guidance and recommendations related to sleep, exercise, nutrition, mental well-being, and radiation awareness.
Korol-on also includes emergency support features such as offline first-aid protocols, space-specific CPR guidance, emergency medical IDs, and medical kit inventory management. Additional features include workout planning, crew information management, health reports, and data export.
Our solution addresses the challenges of maintaining astronauts' physical and mental health in space, where microgravity, radiation, isolation, and limited access to medical assistance create unique risks.
Our goal is to combine health monitoring, preventive care, medical preparedness, and intelligent assistance in one unified platform, helping astronauts stay healthier, safer, and mission-ready.
details:
KOROL-ON – Advanced Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. Project Overview

Korol-on is an astronaut health monitoring and mission support application designed to help astronauts monitor their physical and mental condition during space missions. The platform brings health indicators, medical information, mission data and AI-assisted recommendations together in one place.

The project is inspired by the legacy of Serhiy Korolov and aims to support safer and more informed human space exploration.

2. Main Features

Health Dashboard

The main dashboard provides an overview of an astronaut's health, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), sleep, hydration, stress, energy levels and radiation exposure. A health status indicator helps users quickly understand their current condition.

Korolov-AI Assistant

An integrated AI assistant provides contextual guidance on health indicators, fatigue, sleep, nutrition, exercise, radiation exposure and mental well-being. It can also help users understand their measurements and access relevant emergency information.

Wearable Device Management

The application includes an interface for managing devices such as Garmin Tactix 7 Pro, Polar H10, Oura Ring Gen 4 and RAD-09 Orbital Dosimeter. It displays device status, battery information and sample measurements. The prototype also demonstrates device discovery and manual synchronization.

Health Analytics and History

Users can review historical health measurements through interactive charts. This makes it easier to observe changes in important indicators and compare health data across different periods.

Radiation Exposure Monitoring

A dedicated module displays radiation dose rate and cumulative exposure. Users can monitor exposure levels and configure warning thresholds.

Physical Training and Nutrition

The training module allows astronauts to plan workouts, record exercises and track their training history. The nutrition section helps monitor daily energy intake, protein consumption and hydration.

Mental Well-being

The application includes a guided box-breathing exercise with four breathing phases, each lasting four seconds. It is designed to support relaxation and stress management.

First Aid and Emergency Support

The emergency module includes first-aid protocols, CPR guidance, a CPR metronome, emergency medical information and a medical kit inventory. Users can review available medical supplies and track their quantities and expiration dates.

Crew and Mission Management

The platform includes astronaut profiles, crew information and mission-related data. Users can also export collected information in CSV and JSON formats.

3. Technology and Development

Korol-on was developed using React, JavaScript, JSX/TSX, CSS, Tailwind CSS and Lucide React. The application uses LocalStorage to save data locally in the browser. Interactive charts, interface components and data management functions are implemented within the application.

AI-assisted development tools were used during the development process.

4. Advantages and Project Goals

The main advantage of Korol-on is that it combines multiple aspects of astronaut health monitoring in a single platform. Instead of using separate tools for physical condition, nutrition, training, radiation exposure and emergency information, astronauts can access these features through one interface.

Our goal is to make health information easier to understand, help astronauts notice potentially concerning changes and provide useful guidance during demanding space missions.

5. Current Development Stage and Future Plans

The current version is an interactive prototype demonstrating the main concept and user experience. Some features, including wearable device connections, live telemetry and device synchronization, use simulated data. Authentication is also implemented for demonstration purposes, and the health indicators are not clinically validated.

Future development could include real integrations with Garmin, Polar and Oura devices, physical radiation sensors, secure cloud storage, more advanced AI-based health analysis and shared monitoring for the entire crew and Mission Control.
